title: ScriptServer::scripting_enabled, is assigned too late and causes non tool scripts to run in editor
body:
### Tested versions

Tested in 4.6.1 (mono), but based on the main branch the position of the said enable line is unchanged.
Cachyos (Archlinux).


### System information

Cachyos (Archlinux) - Godot 4.6.1 (mono) & likely master - N/A

### Issue description

Unless I am misunderstanding something, then it appears to me ScriptServer::set_scripting_enabled(false); is used too late for the editor build.
It appears to be what controls if non-tool scripts can run in the editor or not.
This variable above is assigned in editor_node.cpp, but ResourceLoader::add_custom_loaders gets initially invoked by main.cpp before editor_node.cpp is used, meaning scripts initialized during that window will run in the editor when they are not suppose to.

I was working on a ResourceFormatLoader script, it's common functions like _HandlesType did get executed but _Load never did. Most of the time EditorFileSystem::_update_script_classes would force my script to reload which corrected the run-in-editor behavior, but that made me wrongly think that I didn't need the [Tool] attribute, after all the script was loading just fine. That is until I noticed after a while that the script would go dead less than a few 10s of frames into the editor process session.

### Steps to reproduce

#### Behavior
A ResourceFormatLoader script (and likely others) will work in the editor without a Tool attribute for a few 10s of frames, to forever depending on if _update_script_classes executes or not.

#### Expectation
A ResourceFormatLoader script should not work in the editor, unless it has the Tool attribute.

#### Proposed Solution
Move ScriptServer::set_scripting_enabled(false); to execute earlier, possibly directly in main.cpp if in editor mode?

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I have no reason to believe this wouldn't be reproducible in a new project.
Note that I am a C# user, but as far as I can tell the parts in question is shared between languages so it should be applicable to gdscript as well, although I have not tested this.
